Hi all! I'm Anatolii (GitHub: anatoliiohorodnyk). Over the last few days I have been adding formal_proof links for research solved statements. Thanks for merging #6830 (S_n is a Galois group over ℚ)!

Open PRs, from most to least interesting:

  • #6854: the Lovász–Plummer conjecture (lovasz_plummer_conjecture, c = 1/4749). While formalizing it, we found a gap in the published proof (Esperet–Kardoš–King–Král'–Norine, Adv. Math. 2011, Lemma 14, case k = 2). It can be repaired by changing the constants, so the main statement is fine. But the explicit variant with 1/3656 is not supported by the published proof as written. Edmonds' perfect matching polytope theorem and Petersen's theorem were formalized along the way.
  • #6832: Schur's theorem on the Galois group of truncated exponentials.
  • #6834: Pfister's 2ⁿ-squares theorem and Cassels' theorem.
  • #6828: Kaplansky, every power of two is a u-invariant (Springer's theorem).
  • #6821: Erdős 102, the hunter and upper_sqrt variants.
  • #6819: three smaller proofs (Erdős 508, Erdős 184, Agoh–Giuga).

Every proof is checked with leanprover/comparator against the repository statement; the only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proofs were written with Claude (Anthropic); I built the verification pipeline and reviewed the results.

I also found a few statements that look misformalized: junk values of sInf/sSup (Green 22, Erdős 503, Erdős 1180), a two-sided IsBigO in Erdős 30, a statement that depends on a sorry lemma (Erdős 295), and a docstring mismatch in Erdős 513. I'd be happy to open issues — is one issue per type of problem OK?

I know the review queue is long. If another format would make reviewing easier for you, just tell me.
Hey Anatolii, that sounds great! For the already open PRs, I can take a look other the next few days!
For the misformalisations, feel free to open issues (or directly PRs if you want to handle the fixing, and you can request a review from me)
Thanks a lot, Paul! I'll open PRs with the fixes for the misformalised statements over the next days. I'll keep them small — one PR per type of problem — so they're quick to check.
